items.title: Modify splitChunksPlugin to give shared CSS chunks different names
items.body:
I believe this is the fix for the performance regressions for some sites using granular chunks. The previous naming system for shared chunks is causing minSize to get ignored for CSS chunks, because they share the same name as (big enough) JS chunks. This is resulting in the creation of lots of tiny CSS chunks, slowing down initial CSS loading and FCP.

The fix simply modifies the splitChunksPlugin name test so it produces a different name for CSS chunks.

I've only tested this on one app so far--I'll try a few more tomorrow then ping about getting this merged.

items.title: Add initial SSG fallback handling
items.body:
This adds initial support for rendering a loading state when either:

- the page wasn't pre-rendered and is visited directly
- or during a client transition while the page's data is being fetched and we didn't have cached page data available

The currently discussed way to tell if the page should render the loading state is whether the page's props are present or not, although we might iterate on this more later to make it more explicit

While serving the fallback when a page was visited directly without a cached version being available we immediately kick off a request for the data once the page is loaded and then once the page is hydrated and the data is available we render the page with the data

Ref: https://github.com/zeit/next.js/issues/9524

items.title: Remove ts-ignore where possible
items.body:
`ts-ignore` is pretty much a catch-all. I replaced it wherever possible by tweaking types or type casts.
Type casts convey better the "I know for sure this thing will have this type" without throwing away all other type checking on a line.

All code should be functionally unchanged, with the exception of the [`replaceState` second parameter](https://github.com/Janpot/next.js/blob/3f2a8a9c353a89ff1cb8c0958c30feedd470b481/packages/next/next-server/lib/router/router.ts#L464) which I change from `null` to empty string as per https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/History/replaceState
> **title**
> [Most browsers currently ignores this parameter](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/2174), although they may use it in the future. Passing the empty string here should be safe against future changes to the method. Alternatively, you could pass a short title for the state.

items.title: Simplify create-next-app README
items.body:
This PR updates the README file that gets copied when the user runs `create-next-app`.

First, this fixes a bug where README.md file actually was not correctly copied when the user runs `create-next-app`. This was happening because `create-next-app` gets built using `ncc` which in turn uses `webpack-asset-relocator-loader`, which ignores README.md. I renamed the file as README-template.md as a workaround.

I’ve **removed** the following sections because they're mostly covered by Learn and Docs. I think we should keep the README as simple as possible and just point them to docs/learn, instead of adding what's on docs/learn.

- **Available commands:** The only relevant command to get started is `dev`, so I focused on that instead of talking about `build` or `start`.
- **Folder Structure:** Covered in [Learn](https://nextjs.org/learn/basics/getting-started) and [getting started docs](https://nextjs.org/docs/), no need to add it here
- **Using CSS:** Covered in [Learn](https://nextjs.org/learn/basics/styling-components) and [docs](https://nextjs.org/docs/basic-features/built-in-css-support) , no need to add it here
- **Adding Components:** Covered in [Learn](https://nextjs.org/learn/basics/using-shared-components), no need to add it here
- **Fetching data:** Covered in [Learn](https://nextjs.org/learn/basics/fetching-data-for-pages) and [docs](https://nextjs.org/docs/basic-features/data-fetching), no need to add it here
- **Syntax highlighting:** This is not specific to Next.js - seems like it was copied from [create-react-app](https://create-react-app.dev/docs/setting-up-your-editor/#syntax-highlighting) docs
- **Table of Contents:** Because I'm removing most contents from README, it's much shorter now and therefore Table of Contents is unnecessary

Instead, I focused on the three most important things for this README:

- Showing where to start
- Showing how to learn more about Next.js
- Showing how to deploy on ZEIT

items.title: Speculate Navigations for Client-Side JS
items.body:
Our router has a `prefetch` method that accepts an `href` argument. However, other route-related methods accept a `href` and `as` argument.

This pull request unifies the router interface by allowing the user to pass `href` and `as`, like they would to other methods.
It also adds optional options to the end, allowing users to specify if the fetch is [`priority` or not](https://github.com/GoogleChromeLabs/quicklink/blob/836f170df4007c05c24b1300e0faf04fb823168b/src/index.mjs#L47).

On mouse enter, we trigger a higher-priority loading of the page by injecting its `<script>` tags. This makes the files immediately jump to the front of the Network queue, and starts the script parsing early (prior to navigation).

items.title: Support distDir with trailing slash for static files
items.body:
Next.js fails to serve static files when `distDir` option contains a trailing slash. I have narrowed the issue down to `isServeableUrl` in `next-server.ts`:
https://github.com/zeit/next.js/blob/082cc68d87854034e95db371af32717d83bad2f6/packages/next/next-server/server/next-server.ts#L1260-L1272

In particular, the fragment `join(this.distDir) + sep` results in a path with two separators at the end, since `this.distDir` still contains the trailing slash. 

I have fixed the issue by joining `this.distDir` with the path separator, which will not add an extra path separator if the `distDir` already contains a trailing slash. I also have tried to add a regression test for this issue, but have not been able to run it yet.

Fixes #10582

items.title: Add calling getStaticPaths in development before showing fallback
items.body:
This adds calling `getStaticPaths` in development for dynamic SSG pages to determine whether we should show the fallback for a specific request or not and to also help catch any errors that may occur in `getStaticPaths` before doing a production build.

The initial request calls `getStaticPaths` before returning the fallback but subsequent requests use the cached static paths and lazily recheck them so that the user isn't always waiting on their `getStaticPaths`.

We also make sure to call `getStaticPaths` in a separate process to ensure side-effects aren't relied on in development which will not work in production

items.title: Remove `next/link` from Example: With Chakra UI
items.body:
# Why
When the example is run, it'll show an error that tells an invalid `href` in `<Link>` from the `next/link` component.

# Culprit
At first, I thought it has a connection with the Next version in the example dependencies.

But it turns out because, in the example, it used two `Link` components:
- From `next/link`
- From `@chakra-ui/core`

# So
Because the intention from the original creator of the example is to make the link to redirect to another page (not SPA). So I think, removing the `next/link` and only use the `Link` from `@chakra-ui-core` is sufficient. 

## Screenshot
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/27177332/75013444-e3273500-54b6-11ea-9655-cb20541ff877.png)
